title: Cybastion — Angola Telecom digital-sovereignty investment, 2025
description:
"U.S.-based technology firm Cybastion has announced a landmark $170 million investment in partnership with Angola's incumbent telecommunications operator, Angola Telecom E.P., aimed at strengthening the country's digital infrastructure and cybersecurity capacity." The partnership forms part of Cybastion's "Digital Fast Track" initiative.

"As part of the initial implementation, $25 million will be allocated to establish a national cybersecurity agency and launch cybersecurity training programs in collaboration with the Cisco Networking Academy. The investment will also support critical digital infrastructure, including the deployment of undersea cables between Luanda and the port city of Lobito." The deal builds on a memorandum of understanding signed in March 2025 at Mobile World Congress in Barcelona.
scope_basis: Cybersecurity agency and training, subsea cables and digital infrastructure with the telecom operator.

recipient: Angolan Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technology and Mass Communications

The Japanese ambassador and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' International Cooperation Directorate "signed an agreement earlier this week to launch the DTT Broadcasting Network Development Project." "The Japan International Cooperation Agency will undertake the project in collaboration with the Angolan Ministry of Telecommunications, Information Technology, and Mass Communications."
scope_basis: Grant builds a digital terrestrial television transmission network.

financier: Société Générale
title: Société Générale — Angola Earth Observation Satellite System financing, 2025
description: "The agreements, signed with French financial institution Société Générale, allocate €35,268,507 and €189,988,694—totaling €225,257,201—for the design, manufacturing, and launch of an Earth Observation Satellite System. This ambitious project, carried out in partnership with European aerospace leader AIRBUS, includes the construction, launch, and in-orbit installation of the satellite." Signed during the Angola-France Economic Forum concluding the President's state visit.
scope_basis: Finances design, manufacture and launch of an Earth observation satellite system.

title: CDC-CI Capital — Ivorian startup seed programme, 2026
description:
"CDC-CI Capital, the investment arm of Côte d'Ivoire's public deposit and consignment fund, has deployed a further CFA720 million ($1.2 million) into eight local startups, marking the latest salvo in a government-backed campaign to accelerate the country's technology ecosystem and create white-collar jobs for its youthful population."

"The seed grants, ranging from CFA45 million to CFA100 million, were announced on Wednesday at the closing ceremony of the third National Employment and Recruitment Fair (FNER) in Abidjan's Treichville district. The event was presided over by vice-premier and defence minister Téné Birahima Ouattara, and the funds were channeled through a dedicated programme run jointly by CDC-CI Capital and the Youth Employment Agency (Agence Emploi Jeunes)."

"The eight recipients were drawn from the first cohort of the 'Programme d'Appui à l'Écosystème des Startups' — a seeding facility designed to help very young, innovative companies structure their operations, acquire initial customers and position themselves for larger investment rounds. In addition to cash grants, the programme provides mentoring and technical assistance, officials said at the fair."

Three of the eight beneficiaries were disclosed as technology companies: **Ecole Pay**, a school-fee digitisation platform, CFA 100 million; **ADES (Agence de Développement de l'E-Santé)**, operating the UMED telemedicine and home-care network, CFA 100 million; and **Flot**, a mobility startup offering ride-hailing drivers a path to electric-vehicle ownership, CFA 65 million.

"Le programme « Accélération numérique au Cameroun », … doté d'une enveloppe de 9,83 milliards de F, va permettre de renforcer la compétitivité des Très petites, petites et moyennes entreprises." (The "Digital Acceleration in Cameroon" programme, endowed with FCFA 9.83 billion, will strengthen the competitiveness of very small, small and medium enterprises.)

One of three EU-Cameroon grant conventions signed 2026-06-16 in Yaoundé, totalling over FCFA 36 billion. Only this digital-competitiveness slice and the "Digital Business Boost for Africa" slice (2026-06-16-european-union-xca-2026-digital-business-boost-africa) are recorded as deal records; the third convention, "Forêts et cacao durables et compétitifs au Cameroun" (FCFA 17.5bn, forest-wood and cocoa value chains), is out of the wiki's scope and is not recorded.
scope_basis: Digital acceleration programme for small-enterprise competitiveness.

description: "The Ministry of Planning estimates the cost of developing RDC-PASS at $97.1 million. The government launched the project through a public-private partnership signed in June 2025 with Trident Digital Tech DRC Africa SAS, a subsidiary of Singapore-based Trident Digital Tech Holdings. The agreement grants the company exclusive rights to provide electronic know-your-customer (e-KYC) services for 20 years." RDC-PASS supports biometric SIM registration, unified e-government access via a single digital identifier, automated e-KYC for financial institutions, and issuance of secure digital identities. It forms part of a broader government plan to invest $1 billion in digital development between 2026 and 2030. RDC-PASS was officially launched in Kinshasa under President Félix Tshisekedi on 13 June 2026.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: Eastcastle Debt II — shared telecom tower infrastructure, DR Congo
description:
Eastcastle Infrastructure DRC SARLU (Eastcastle DRC or the Company) is a subsidiary of Eastcastle Infrastructure Limited (Eastcastle Infrastructure), which was established in 2020 as a platform company to own and operate shared telecom tower infrastructure in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Nigeria. Eastcastle Infrastructure and Eastcastle DRC are existing IFC clients, with environmental and social (E&S) performance assessed as satisfactory. An Environmental and Social Review Summary (ESRS) for IFC's initial equity investment in Eastcastle Infrastructure was publicly disclosed in 2021 (https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/44090/eastcastle). IFC subsequently disclosed an ESRS in connection with a further US$30 million debt facility provided to Eastcastle DRC in 2023 (https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/46563/eastcastle-debt).

The development impact thesis derives from the Company's potential to enhance mobile broadband capacity for MNOs in the DRC to help improve quality of connectivity for end users and mitigate environmental impact through infrastructure sharing and energy mix strategy. Beyond the Company, this initiative is anticipated to strengthen competitiveness in the tower sharing market.
scope_basis: Debt facility for a shared telecom tower company.

title: Algebra Ventures — Blnk consumer-lending fintech raise, 2026
description: "Blnk, an Egyptian fintech that enables consumers to request loans during point-of-sale (PoS) checkouts, has raised $37.1 million in equity and debt financing to expand its lending to consumers with little or no formal access to credit. The raise includes a $12.5 million Series A equity round led by Algebra Ventures, with participation from SANAD Fund for MSME, Endeavor Catalyst, and existing investor Emirates International Investment Company. Blnk also secured $24.6 million in local currency debt facilities from banks and non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), including National Bank of Egypt, Suez Canal Bank, and Bank Al Baraka Egypt." Blnk said it will use the funding to expand its lending products, strengthen its technology, and explore growth beyond its current markets.
scope_basis: Equity in a consumer-lending fintech.

financier: eFinance for Digital and Financial Investments S.A.E.
title: eFinance — acquisition of Tamweely Financial Services, 2026
description:
"eFinance, an EFG Holding company and the leading investment bank in the Middle East and North Africa, announced today that its Investment Banking division acted as sole financial advisor to eFinance for Digital and Financial Investments S.A.E. ('eFinance' or the 'Group') on its proposed full acquisition of Tamweely Financial Services ('Tamweely'), a leading Egyptian non-bank financial services provider focused on micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises ('MSMEs')."

"By combining Tamweely's established MSME lending platform with eFinance's technology, data, and distribution capabilities, the Group is positioned to capture more value from the economic activity flowing through its ecosystem and unlock new opportunities across recurring financial services revenues, embedded finance, and data-led lending."

"The consideration combines cash, newly issued eFinance shares, and performance-linked earnout consideration, including approximately 146.1 million new shares, representing around 4.0% of the enlarged share capital, alongside upfront cash consideration of up to EGP 956.4 million."

"Completion remains subject to customary conditions and approvals, including eFinance's Extraordinary General Meeting and relevant regulatory approvals, including those of the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA). Closing is expected in the second half of 2026, subject to the satisfaction of applicable conditions precedent."
scope_basis: Acquired company is a conventional small-business lender; the digital element is the acquirer's technology and planned data-led lending.

financier: Hassan Allam
title: Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure — Egypt data-centre licence and investment, 2026
description: "Egypt's telecom regulator has awarded a new data center license to Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure and Data Center Solutions for a project backed by an initial investment of $400 million." "The National Telecom Regulatory Authority (NTRA) granted a license on Monday, May 15, to Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure and Data Center Solutions to build and operate a data center in the country. The company is developing the project in partnership with technology firm A15 and plans to invest an initial $400 million during the first phase." The facility will provide data hosting, cloud computing and AI-ready infrastructure for government agencies, financial institutions and businesses; it is the tenth data-centre licence issued in Egypt in two years.
scope_basis: Investment builds and operates a data centre offering hosting, cloud and AI-ready infrastructure.

financier: Partech Africa
title: Partech - Synapse Analytics Series A, 2026
description: "Synapse Analytics, an AI company that builds agentic decisioning infrastructure for regulated financial institutions putting policy control directly in the hands of credit and risk teams, announced today that it has raised US$13 million in a Series A funding round, bringing the total raised to US$17 million since inception. Terms of the transaction and valuation were not disclosed. The round was led by Partech, a global technology investment firm, with additional participation from Algebra Ventures and Silicon Badia. The new capital will be used to scale the team, accelerate product development and expand international market reach."

financier: World Bank
title: Governance Modernization to Enable Efficient Service Delivery Project
description: To improve government capacity to manage public resources efficiently and increase transparency and accountability of service delivery. The development objective of the Governance Modernization to Enable Efficient Service Delivery Project for Ethiopia is to improve government institutional capacity to mobilize and manage public financial and human resources efficiently. The project comprises of four components. The first component, improving public administration capabilities will focus on three fundamental building blocks aligned with the Government of Ethiopia (GoE's) draft Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda (HGER) 2.0, civil service reform roadmap and civil service policy. It consists of following sub-components: (i) developing an evidence-based and data-informed approach to human resource management; (ii) competency-based human resource management; (iii) institutionalizing training, capacity building, and change management; and (iv) reform innovation facility. The second component, improving domestic revenue mobilization capabilities will support the GoE in implementing key tax administration reforms to help it achieve the national medium term revenue strategy. It consists of following sub-components: (i) leveraging technology and data analytics to support risk-based tax administration; and (ii) improving the quality and availability of taxpayer services. The third component, improving public financial management capabilities will support the GoE in scaling up the use of technology, addressing critical deficiencies along the public financial management (PFM) cycle, the professionalization of accountants and procurement professionals within the public service, and the institutionalization of core training and government-to-government capacity building. It consists of following sub-components: (i) scaling up the use of technology for improved public financial management; (ii) address critical public financial management deficiencies; and (iii) institutionalizing professional training, capacity building, and change management. The fourth component, project management will support the management, coordination, and monitoring and evaluation (M and E) of project activities and funds.
scope_basis: Governance project; technology for tax and financial management sits beside civil service human resource reform and training.

This second debt tranche supports Safaricom Ethiopia's continued expansion of its 4G/5G network, M-PESA mobile money platform, and broadband connectivity infrastructure across Ethiopia. The Company plans to invest over $8 billion in Ethiopia over 10 years. This follows IFC's first $100M A-loan in 2023.

**US$1.1 billion equivalent over a three-year period (2026–2028)**, announced by MTN Group
President and CEO Ralph Mupita at a media interaction in Accra on **2026-02-20** during a
three-day working visit, and published by MTN Ghana on **2026-02-23**: "We are going to
accelerate capital investment within the business, US$1.1 billion equivalent over a three-year

customer experience, under MTN's Ambition/Mission 2030 strategy. **US$380 million of it is
stated for 2026**, alongside ~800 new network sites (MTN Ghana CEO Stephen Blewett, 30th
anniversary launch, MTN House Accra, 2026-05-14; restated 2026-07-31). The announcing party
denominates in USD-equivalent in its own words while reporting in cedi.

*This record was built 2026-07-23 from a Daily Graphic report of a 2026-07-20 statement by
MTN Ghana's Chief Home Officer Richard Acheampong putting the figure at "US$1 billion" for
digital infrastructure with no timeframe. **Reconcile, 2026-08-01, resolved that against the
company primary**: the US$1bn is MTN's **superseded five-year prior**, and the July restatement
of it does not describe a second commitment (see* `## Notes`*). The legacy* `deal_id`
*(`mtn-gha-fibre-home-2026`) and filename are kept unchanged so existing links hold, though the
programme is wider than fibre and home broadband.*

A growing area of concern in Kenya, TFGBV has far-reaching impacts on the rights, safety, and participation of individuals in digital and offline spaces, particularly women and girls. The 2022 General Elections in Kenya saw a dramatic increase in GBV (including TFGBV), and as the 2027 General Elections in Kenya approach, this project is timely and needed to support inclusive online civic engagement and to support the prevention of TFGBV amongst marginalised communities.Targeting informal settlements in Nairobi, Kiambu, Machakos, and Kajiado counties, this project will directly support communities most at risk and vulnerable to digital abuse in the lead up to the 2027 Elections, and learnings from this project can be shared with the Embassy’s other partners working on youth and women civic engagement.

Paragraph 2.5.9.1 of the *Cooperation Framework between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Kenya on Health*: "The U.S. Government intends to provide $175,000,000 over the course of the Framework to support data systems. The Government of Kenya intends to continue investing in the Digital Superhighway."

Appendix 1 gives the annual split of the data-systems line: **US$30,000,000 (2026), US$75,000,000 (2027), US$50,000,000 (2028), US$10,000,000 (2029), US$10,000,000 (2030)** — US fiscal years, 15 October to 30 September.

Paragraph 2.5.9.4 records that the amount covers developers, product managers and systems engineers, cloud computing capacity and software licences, and hardware. Paragraph 2.5.9.5 leaves ongoing licensing, cloud, and hardware maintenance and replacement costs not specifically paid by the US Government to Kenya.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: ATK Debt II — Atlas Tower Kenya mobile tower expansion
description:
The proposed transaction is a multi-currency senior debt financing of up to US$30 million, including an IFC A Loan of up to US$20 million and remaining to be mobilized from a B Lender/parallel lender for Atlas Tower Kenya (ATK or the Company), an IFC client since 2021. The funding will (i) enable ATK to build and operate new macro towers in Kenya, expanding its existing portfolio of 442 towers; (ii) support ATK's Green Power Program which involves the large-scale deployment of solar power, battery storage, and off-grid or hybrid energy solutions to help reduce dependence on grid electricity and diesel; and (iii) refinance existing indebtedness (Project). ATK is an independent telecommunications infrastructure company operating in Kenya under a build-to-suit (BTS) model. Established in 2018, ATK owns and operates a portfolio of 442 towers and manages the full tower lifecycle, including site identification, land leasing, permitting, construction, energy solutions, and operations and maintenance.

The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase the capacity of mobile networks in Kenya, resulting in improved access to quality connectivity for individuals and businesses. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will deepen the competitiveness of the mobile tower market in Kenya by expanding shared infrastructure integrating green power solutions via competition channels.
scope_basis: Loan to a telecom tower company for new towers, tower power and refinancing.

UNCDF "absorbs a share of the credit risk on eligible loans Co-op Bank extends to qualifying digital businesses — covering 50 per cent of the outstanding principal, rising to 70 per cent for borrowers in Kenya's Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs)." Co-op Bank originates, assesses and manages all loans. The facility forms part of the Digital Platforms Kenya (DigiKen) Programme, implemented by UNESCO (lead), UNCDF, UN Women and UNEP with the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy and support from the Joint SDG Fund. Launched in Nairobi, reported 24 September 2026.
scope_basis: Guarantee restricted to loans to digital businesses.

financier: World Bank
title: Morocco Second Identity and Targeting for Social Protection Project
description: The PDO is to support the expansion of the coverage of the Digital Civil and Social Identifier (DCSID) for the Moroccan population and foreign residents and the strengthening of the inclusion of NPR and SR — including in rural and remote areas — to improve the targeting and access to social protection programs. The project aims to support the development of key building blocks of a modern, adaptative and efficient social protection system. The project will support the national rollout of the National Population Registry (Registre National de la Population – RNP) to provide a trusted source of identity and an accurate digital authentication of individuals using the Civil and Social Digital Identifier (IDCS). In addition, the RNP design incorporates services such as digital authentication and electronic “know-your-customer” (eKYC) services. The new services will contribute to extending the usefulness of the system and establish the basis for a modern, digital platform for citizens and residents to verify their identity in a remote and paperless form, which can be used across social programs and beyond.The Project will also support the implementation of the Unified Social Registry (Registre Social Unifie – RSU) as a unique gateway for all SSN in Morocco. The RSU will provide reliable socio-economic information on households to estimate the level of consumption per household member and, on this basis, identify the applicants who are eligible for SSN programs. The RSU constitutes the first level of the universal and adaptative social protection system and will improve the targeting of SSN programs, reduce fraud and error, including duplicate or ghost beneficiaries.
scope_basis: Finances the population registry, digital identifier and social registry systems.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: Morocco – Promoting innovation and the development of the insurtech ecosystem
description: The Moroccan InsurTech, Inclusion and Innovation Programme (PM3I) is a technical assistance operation designed to foster innovation and strengthen the InsurTech ecosystem in Morocco in order to expand insurance inclusion and improve customer experience, particularly for underserved and vulnerable population groups. The total cost of the project amounts to USD 680,000, of which USD 510,000 is financed through a grant from the Africa Digital Financial Inclusion Facility (ADFI) managed by the African Development Bank, while the remaining USD 170,000 is provided as a counterpart contribution by the Supervisory Authority of Insurance and Social Welfare (ACAPS). The project is implemented nationwide in Morocco, with ACAPS acting as the executing agency, and aligns with Morocco’s National Financial Inclusion Strategy and the New Development Model, while benefiting from ADFI’s broader multi-donor platform supported by partners such as the Gates Foundation, AFD, the Government of Luxembourg, the Government of India and We-Fi. The objective of the project is to promote innovation and the development of a robust and inclusive InsurTech ecosystem in Morocco in order to improve access to insurance services and enhance the quality, affordability and relevance of insurance products for vulnerable groups, especially women. The programme seeks to strengthen the regulatory and market monitoring framework, support the emergence of innovative and technology-enabled insurance solutions, and improve the alignment between insurance supply and demand through participatory diagnostics and co-creation of use cases. By reinforcing regulatory capacity, encouraging experimentation and innovation, and supporting change management within the insurance sector, the project aims to create an enabling environment for inclusive insurance, increase trust in insurance services, and contribute to greater financial resilience against economic and climate-related shocks. The beneficiaries of the project include the insurance regulator (ACAPS), 25 insurance companies, around 2,000 intermediaries and brokers, and approximately 30 InsurTech project promoters, whose capacities will be strengthened through regulatory support, training, tools and innovation programmes. The project is expected to directly benefit about 200,000 new insurance users, including at least 100,000 women, as well as 30,000 microenterprises and cooperatives, with a minimum of 40 percent owned or led by women. scope_basis: Technical assistance to develop the insurtech ecosystem.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: Morocco – Grant project for the establishment of an acquisition fund to facilitate
description: The Africa Digital Financial Inclusion Initiative (ADFI) grant responds to crucial challenges defined by the Central Bank of Morocco at both the national and sector levels. Although Morocco has made significant strides in the development of digital infrastructure and the adoption of technologies, major challenges remain, including the limited use of electronic payments, the heavy reliance on cash, and the weight of the informal economy, representing about a third of GDP. These obstacles hinder the financial inclusion of vulnerable segments of the population, women, young people, and rural populations. Against this backdrop, the project aims at accelerating the transition to digital payments while expanding access to financial services tailored to the needs of all. It helps to bridge the gap between the country's growing technological capabilities, such as high smartphone and Internet penetration, as well as their low use for digital payments. In addition, it plays a key role in mitigating economic risks by reinforcing the integration of marginalized populations into the formal economy, and by developing secure mechanisms such as digital transfers and micro-insurance. Through the African Development Bank, ADFI brings a unique added value through its ability to mobilize dedicated financial resources and coordinate public and private stakeholders. The project seeks to accelerate digital financial inclusion by lowering barriers to entry for merchants, fostering trust in digital payment systems. It combines financial incentives, awareness-raising campaigns, and sound project management practices to create an enabling ecosystem where merchants—particularly women—can adopt and use digital financial services at scale. The project aims at fostering robust and sustainable digital financial inclusion by supporting the development of an electronic payment acceptance network for merchants. The project aims at achieving two specific objectives : (i) developing electronic payments; and (ii) encouraging their adoption to reduce the circulation of cash in Morocco. It seeks to financially include excluded segments of the population, especially recipients of government aid, by creating cases for the use of electronic funds to avoid mass cash withdrawals. At the same time, the project aims at establishing a larger and more profitable electronic payment ecosystem for market players, while democratising these payments through communication and financial education initiatives. scope_basis: Grant to accelerate merchant adoption of digital payments.

financier: Sida
title: Mali RGPH5 census — special review, Swedish contribution
description:
The Malian general census takes place every 10 years. The fifth census was planned to take place 2016-2021 with 2019 being the year when most of the work will be implemented. The process was delayed and concluded 2022. The census is a large and complicated project in a vast country like Mali that has limited infrastructure and security challenges. The census will produce data that will be used for social and economic development in the country and to follow up on development interventions.

The Swedish contribution will be used by the Malian government to co-fund the fifth population census (RGPH5) in Mali. By Malian law and according to UN recommendations these are to take place every 10 years. The census is not a sample but a complete inventory of people and their accommodation in Mali. The census will provide data and analyses on: 1) total number of inhabitants in Mali and structure by sex and age 2) spatial distribution of people according to administrative unites and type of residence 3) social, economic and cultural characteristics of the Malian population 4) level, structure and tendencies regarding fertility, civil status, mortality and migration 5) indicators for lobbying regarding vulnerable groups, especially old people, women, young people, people living with handicaps, displaced people, orphans etc 6) conclusions regarding the evolution of the data above since the 1976 census 7) projections and demographic prospects into the future 8) characteristics of households, habitat and livelihoods 9) analysis and cartography of poverty 10) updated statistics on villages, wells and other collective social infrastructure 11) geo-referenced information on collective social infrastructure and economic units 12) establishment of demographic indicators 13) capacity building on data collection, analysis and communication using modern information technology The intervention produces baseline information and analyses that are crucial to the design of development action,
scope_basis: Contribution co-funds the national population census.

title: Integrating upSCALE into the Ministry of Health [Mozambique]
description:
upSCALE is an electronic community health information system (eCHIS). The eCHIS software is uploaded onto a mobile phone and provided to the community health workers known locally as Agentes polivalentes de saúde (APSs). It is designed to improve quality of care and enhance reporting rates to improve data for decision making.

The project started in 2016 as a pilot and has since scaled up. This current UNICEF grant started in January 2025 with the aim of institutionalising upSCALE into the Ministry of Health through data ownership and data-informed decision-making for the community health programme.

Through this grant, upSCALE will be scaled up to all 10 provinces covering all districts in each province and equipping every APS with a digital device.
scope_basis: Scales up an electronic community health information system and equips health workers with digital devices.

description:
"2.5.3 Funding Plan: The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $16,666,385; 2027 $28,230,116; 2028 $18,533,429; 2029 $11,129,710; 2030 $8,512,439."

The money builds SIS-RME (the integrated electronic medical record absorbing the US-built SESP patient tracking system, transferred to Mozambican management by 2026-06-20), SIS-LAB, the eVIDR outbreak surveillance platform, nSIMAM commodity logistics, a health data exchange due functional by end-2026 and a national health data warehouse due operational by end-2027. "Development of data systems funded by the U.S. Government are expected to be fully led and owned by the Government of Mozambique with technical assistance and workplan oversight by the U.S. Government" (2.5.1). The US reserves the right to "revisit its funding levels" if no mutually acceptable technology roadmap is agreed (2.5.3).

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$1,829,380,000 against Mozambique's US$70,573,106 (Appendix 1). Non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement" (6.9).
scope_basis: The line funds health data systems: electronic medical records, laboratory, surveillance, logistics and a data warehouse.

title: KOICA - INGD Mozambique, ICT equipment for disaster risk management, 2026
description:
Verbatim press release, Programa das Nacoes Unidas para o Desenvolvimento, 9 September 2026:

COMUNICADO DE IMPRENSA

PNUD e KOICA reforçam a capacidade de Moçambique para a gestão do risco de desastres

Maputo, 9 de Setembro de 2026

– O Programa das Nações Unidas para o

Desenvolvimento (PNUD), em parceria com o Governo de Moçambique e com o apoio

financeiro da Agência de Cooperação Internacional da Coreia (KOICA)

, procedeu hoje à

entrega de equipamento de tecnologias de informação e comunicação (TIC), avaliado em

mais de 300 mil dólares norte

-americanos, com vista a reforçar a capacidade de

Moçambique para antecipar, preparar -se e responder a desastres e outros ch

oques

relacionados com o clima.

A cerimónia de entrega, realizada nas instalações do Instituto Nacional de Gestão e Redução do Risco de Desastres (INGD), em Maputo, assinala mais um marco na implementação do projecto “Promoção da Resiliência aos Desastres e da Coesão Social no Norte e Centro de Moçambique”, lançado em Junho de 2023.

O equipamento inclui computadores portáteis e de mesa, impressoras, sistemas de videoconferência e outros recursos tecnológicos. Estes meios irão apoiar o INGD e outras instituições governamentais envolvidas na gestão do risco de desastres, através do reforço da gestão da informação, da comunicação, da coordenação e dos processos de tomada de decisão aos níveis nacional, provincial e distrital.

O investimento beneficiará directamente equipas técnicas nas províncias de Cabo Delgado, Niassa, Nampula, Sofala e Manica, reforçando as capacidades tecnológicas e institucionais necessárias para coordenar a preparação e resposta a desastres, ao mesmo tempo que promove decisões mais céleres e baseadas em evidências.

A entrega do equipamento reflecte um compromisso mais amplo do Governo de Moçambique, do PNUD e da República da Coreia com o fortalecimento dos sistemas e capacidades nacionais para a construção da resiliência.

Intervindo na cerimónia, Sua Excelência Bok -Wan Kang, Embaixador da República da Coreia em Moçambique, sublinhou que o valor desta parceria vai muito além da simples disponibilização de equipamento.

“Não se trata apenas de fornecer equipamento; trata -se de garantir um apoio contínuo para enfrentar desafios reais, reforçando a preparação para desastres e as capacidades locais.”

COMUNICADO DE IMPRENSA

O diplomata destacou a importância de uma cooperação para o desenvolvimento orientada para resultados concretos, que combine apoio financeiro com conhecimento, tecnologia e experiência.

“A resiliência sustentável constrói -se não apenas através de infra -estruturas e sistemas, mas também por meio de parcerias mais fortes e comunidades capacitadas. Quando a tecnologia e os equipamentos adequados são disponibilizados e utilizados de forma prática através da nossa cooperação, podemos salvar vidas, proteger meios de subsistência e reforçar a resiliência das comunidades vulneráveis.”

O Embaixador reafirmou ainda o compromisso da República da Coreia em continuar a trabalhar com Moçambique como parceiro de confiança e expressou a sua gratidão ao Governo de Moçambique, ao INGD, ao PNUD e ao Escritório da KOICA em Moçambique pela colaboraç ão contínua.

Para o PNUD, este investimento representa uma contribuição concreta para o reforço das capacidades nacionais antes da ocorrência de crises. O Representante Residente Adjunto para Programas do PNUD Moçambique, Cleophas Torori, salientou que uma gestão eficaz do risco de desastres exige que as instituições disponham dos sistemas, da informação e dos instrumentos necessários para antecipar riscos e actuar atempadamente.

“Reforçar a resiliência aos desastres não significa apenas responder eficazmente quando

ocorre uma crise. Significa assegurar que as instituições disponham da informação, dos

sistemas, dos instrumentos e das capacidades necessárias para antecipar riscos, t

omar

decisões informadas e agir precocemente.”

Acrescentou ainda: “A informação fiável e uma gestão eficaz da informação são elementos fundamentais da moderna gestão do risco de desastres.”

O equipamento apoiará, por conseguinte, muito mais do que as operações institucionais quotidianas. O seu objectivo é reforçar os sistemas através dos quais a informação é produzida, partilhada e utilizada para apoiar a prevenção, preparação, resposta e rec uperação.

“O verdadeiro valor deste investimento será medido, em última instância, não pelo equipamento em si, mas pelas capacidades institucionais e pelos serviços públicos que permitirá desenvolver”, afirmou o Sr. Torori.

COMUNICADO DE IMPRENSA

O responsável sublinhou igualmente a importância de assegurar a manutenção adequada

do equipamento e a sua integração efectiva nos sistemas institucionais e nas práticas de

trabalho, de modo a garantir benefícios sustentáveis para além do momento da entreg

a.

Ao receber o equipamento, a Presidente do INGD, Luisa Meque , considerou o apoio uma importante contribuição para o fortalecimento do sistema nacional de gestão do risco de desastres e da capacidade institucional para actuar de forma mais eficaz entre sectores e diferentes níveis de governação.

A dirigente descreveu a parceria com a KOICA como um exemplo de cooperação prática que fortalece as capacidades nacionais através do acesso ao conhecimento e à tecnologia.

“Com este gesto, estamos perante uma parceria inteligente em que todos saímos mais fortalecidos. A Coreia partilha a sua experiência e conhecimento, enquanto Moçambique reforça o seu acesso a conhecimento e tecnologia que nos permitem melhorar a forma como monitorizamos e gerimos eventos climáticos extremos e complexos, alguns dos quais agravados pela variabilidade e pelas mudanças climáticas.”

A Presidente reafirmou ainda o compromisso do INGD em assegurar a utilização eficaz do equipamento e em prosseguir os esforços para reduzir a vulnerabilidade das comunidades expostas a eventos extremos.

Moçambique encontra -se cada vez mais exposto a múltiplos riscos interligados, incluindo ciclones, cheias, secas, choques relacionados com o clima, deslocações populacionais e outros factores susceptíveis de agravar vulnerabilidades sociais e económicas.

O projecto responde a estes desafios através de uma abordagem integrada que reconhece as ligações entre riscos climáticos, vulnerabilidade aos desastres, coesão social e instabilidade.

Implementado pelo PNUD, o projecto visa reforçar a capacidade das instituições e das

comunidades para antecipar, resistir e recuperar de choques e crises, contribuindo

simultaneamente para prevenir novos ciclos de vulnerabilidade, conflito e instabilidade.

A

iniciativa reúne instituições nacionais, autoridades locais, parceiros de desenvolvimento e

comunidades em torno de um objectivo comum: reforçar a resiliência, proteger os ganhos

de desenvolvimento e criar condições para um desenvolvimento mais inclusiv

oe

sustentável.

COMUNICADO DE IMPRENSA
No âmbito desta abordagem, o projecto tem igualmente apoiado o desenvolvimento de capacidades institucionais e de coordenação, incluindo a colaboração com importantes parceiros governamentais, como o Ministério da Justiça, Assuntos Constitucionais e Religiosos, o Serviço Nacional Público de Salvamento (SENSAP) e o Instituto Nacional de Acção Social (INAS).
O investimento em TIC complementa estes esforços ao reforçar a infra -estrutura digital e de informação necessária para apoiar uma coordenação eficaz e processos de tomada de decisão mais eficientes.
Esta entrega ocorre igualmente num momento importante para os esforços de Moçambique no reforço da digitalização das instituições e dos serviços públicos. Um melhor acesso à tecnologia e sistemas de informação mais eficazes podem ajudar as instituições a m elhorar a monitoria dos riscos, a comunicação entre diferentes níveis de governação e a transformação da informação em acções oportunas.
Para o PNUD, a iniciativa demonstra igualmente o valor de parcerias que articulam resiliência, fortalecimento institucional, coesão social e desenvolvimento sustentável.
“Esta é a primeira intervenção apoiada pela KOICA que reúne, numa única iniciativa, as dimensões da resiliência aos desastres e da coesão social”, observou o Sr. Torori. “Vemos esta iniciativa não apenas como um investimento importante para Moçambique, mas também como uma oportunidade para gerar conhecimento, demonstrar boas práticas e orientar futuras abordagens integradas de resiliência e desenvolvimento.”
O PNUD e a KOICA continuarão a trabalhar estreitamente com o Governo de Moçambique para consolidar a implementação do projecto, sistematizar as lições aprendidas e maximizar o seu impacto no desenvolvimento. Em última análise, a ambição partilhada desta pa rceria é clara: instituições mais fortes, decisões mais bem informadas, comunidades mais resilientes e maior coesão social.
A entrega hoje realizada constitui um investimento concreto para alcançar essa visão comum, contribuindo para que os cidadãos, as instituições e os ganhos de desenvolvimento de Moçambique estejam mais preparados para enfrentar os riscos do futuro.

sustainable value chains €60m, education and skills €50m — totalling €178 million,

prose source rather than as a separate digital record because its stated purpose
("to prepare Mozambican students for a digital and sustainable economy") is not specific
enough to a digital activity to map cleanly.

description: EIB loan of EUR 15 million financing construction, construction-monitoring/auditing and Tier III certification (Uptime Institute) of Mauritania's first national data centre in Nouakchott (1,372 m², 100 racks per the AMI account). It will be operated by International Mauritania Telecom (IMT/GIE), combining the state (via Mauripost) with the country's three telecom operators. "The total project cost, financed by the European Investment Bank and supported by the European Union, is estimated at more than €43.5 million, of which €25.6 million is allocated to execution and €17.9 million to maintenance over a 25-year period."
scope_basis: Financing connects Mauritania to a submarine cable, covering execution and maintenance.

financier: World Bank
title: World Bank/IDA — Governance to Enable Service Delivery Project 2.0 (GESD 2), Malawi, 2026
description:
Successor to the Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project, which closed on
30 June 2026. Per the Minister of Finance, Economic Planning and Decentralisation presenting
the ratification bill, GESD 2 "strengthens efficiency in financial resource management and
multi-level governance so that our district and municipal councils can deliver better
services", continuing the performance-based grant system that rewards councils demonstrating
transparency, accountability and effective service delivery. Councils that participated in the
previous GESD Project continue to receive performance-based grants; four municipal councils —
**Karonga, Kasungu, Luchenza and Mangochi** — enter the programme for the first time.

The ratifying legislation (Bill No. 8 of 2026) authorises withdrawals from the IDA financing,
charges all payments under the agreement on the Consolidated Fund, and exempts the grant funds
from taxes, charges and other restrictions under Malawian law.
scope_basis: Text describes performance-based grants to local councils and names no digital component.

financier: World Bank
recipient: Federal Government of Nigeria / BRIDGE Project company
title: World Bank (IDA) — Nigeria BRIDGE nationwide broadband fibre project, 2025
description: "Nigeria has begun the financial advisory process for its ambitious plan to deploy 90,000 kilometres of fibre-optic cable under the $2 billion Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth (BRIDGE) Project, supported by the World Bank." "As part of the agreement with the Bank, which has already approved $500 million in financing, the government is required to appoint a financial advisory firm." "The BRIDGE Project, approved by the World Bank Group Board of Directors on October 8, 2025... Funding will be disbursed in five tranches, with the first $150 million going toward the company's initial equity capitalisation." The financing agreement with IDA was signed 30 December 2025; the Federal Government holds a 49% stake channelled through the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI). The programme deploys about 90,000 km of fibre "built around seven national rings, 37 metropolitan loops, 77 regional networks, and multiple edge data centers" (We Are Tech Africa), narrowing the broadband gap in underserved regions.

title: Airtel Nigeria — Eko Atlantic 38MW hyperscale data centre, 2025
description:
"Airtel Nigeria plans to build a carrier-neutral 38MW hyperscale data centre in Eko Atlantic City in Lagos to meet surging demand for cloud and AI services. financier: Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
title: EAIF — WIOCC senior secured loan for Nigerian fibre-to-the-home, 2025
description:
Verbatim from the financier's own release:

> London, December 15: The Emerging Africa & Asia Infrastructure Fund (EAAIF), a Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) company, managed by Ninety One, today announced a $15 million investment in West Indian Ocean Cable Company (WIOCC), a key pan-African telecommunications infrastructure provider.

> EAAIF’s portion of the funding will support the rollout of fibre to the home networks in Nigeria, addressing the country’s rapidly growing demand for reliable, high-speed internet.

> All financing arrangements, including EAAIF’s $15 million senior secured loan facility, have a 10-year tenor and are structured as sustainability-linked facilities.
scope_basis: Loan funds fibre-to-the-home rollout by a telecom infrastructure provider.

financier: Equinix
title: Equinix LG3 Lagos New Data Centre — $22 Million Investment
description: Equinix announced in November 2025 plans to build LG3, its first newly-constructed data centre in West Africa, at a cost of US$22 million. Set to open in Q1 2026, LG3 is the first phase of a US$100 million investment plan to transform Africa's digital landscape over the next two years. LG3 is located in Lagos, Nigeria and will deliver new colocation capacity supporting Nigeria's strategic position as an international hub for subsea cable connections. The $100 million plan includes expansions at existing sites in Nigeria, Ghana, and Côte d'Ivoire, as well as a new facility in Port Harcourt (PR1) serving as a 2Africa cable landing station.
scope_basis: Investment plan for new and expanded data centres.

financier: European Union
title: European Union — Nigeria Digital Economy Package (connectivity, DPI, skills), 2025
description: "Nigeria has secured a major boost for its digital transformation agenda as the European Commission announced a €45 million commitment under the EU–Nigeria Digital Economy Package. The announcement was made on Tuesday in Brussels during the EU–Nigeria Digital Open Day". Discussions focused on three areas: "Secure Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure" (nationwide fibre backbone, subsea cable capacity, 5G, last-mile access); "e-Governance and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)" (digital identity systems, interoperability frameworks, e-payment infrastructure); and "Digital Skills and Talent Development" (the 3MTT programme).
scope_basis: Digital economy package covering connectivity, digital public infrastructure and digital skills.

financier: U.S. Department of State
recipient: Federal Republic of Nigeria / Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
title: U.S. Department of State — Nigeria health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
Section 2.5.3: "The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $60,000,000; 2027 $49,000,000; 2028 $42,000,000; 2029 $23,000,000; 2030 $22,000,000", against Nigerian co-funding of $13,793,103 (2026) rising to $33,817,048 (2030). In 2026 the US line includes "$1.35M for NigeriaMRS, $1.05M for LAMISPlus, $0.38M for ViVA EMR".

The target is the Nigeria Digital Health Architecture's three exchanges - health information, health services and health insurance claims - into which government EHRs, TB and HIV systems, the National Data Repository, the LMIS, state EHRs and SORMAS are expected to integrate (2.5.1). The US also supports National Health Insurance Authority partnership with US firms "(i.e. AWS)" for data warehousing and cloud storage of the NHIA claims database.

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$1,953,530,560 against Nigeria's US$2,975,634,499 (Appendix 1). Non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement" (6.9). The text is stamped NOT FOR PUBLIC RELEASE on every page.
scope_basis: The recorded sum is the data-systems line of the health agreement, covering health information exchanges and records systems.

description: The Digital Value Chain Infrastructure for Boosting Employment (D-VIBE) Project is a nationwide digital infrastructure initiative in Nigeria designed to expand broadband connectivity, strengthen digital inclusion, and support productivity, jobs, and access to services across key sectors such as agri...
scope_basis: Nationwide digital infrastructure project to expand broadband connectivity and digital inclusion.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: African Development Bank — Nigeria Project BRIDGE (D-VIBE) fibre expansion, 2026
description:
"The African Development Bank (AfDB) has approved a US$200 million loan towards Nigeria's Digital Value Chain Infrastructure for Boosting Employment (D-VIBE) project, also known as Project Bridge, a fiber-optic program aimed at expanding broadband access as well as strengthening the country's digital economy."

"The loan will help Africa's most populous country deploy 90,000km of open-access fiber nationwide, expand digital skills and drive job creation... extending Nigeria's national fiber backbone from around 30,000km to about 120,000km, connecting all 774 local government areas."

"The bank said the loan is part of an $800 million sovereign financing package for the project, alongside $500 million from the World Bank and $100 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). It added that the total project financing is estimated at $2 billion, and includes an EU grant of €22 million, a $2.6 million Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance (MCDF) project preparation grant, and at least $1.2 billion investment from the private sector."
scope_basis: Loan for a national open-access fibre programme with digital skills.

financier: AfricInvest
title: AfricInvest FIVE leads growth round in BFREE pan-African credit management fintech
description: AfricInvest's Financial Inclusion Vehicle (FIVE) leads a growth round in BFREE, a Lagos-based pan-African technology-enabled platform focused on acquisition and servicing of non-performing unsecured retail and SME loan portfolios. BFREE uses proprietary data infrastructure and AI-powered credit risk management to help financial institutions manage distressed credit. Managing over 10 million borrower accounts across 35+ transactions at time of investment. Co-investors include Algebra Ventures (first Nigeria investment), Capria Ventures, VestedWorld, Axian CVC, Angaza Capital, 4Di Capital, and DotExe Ventures.
scope_basis: Equity in a technology-enabled credit management fintech.

financier: CardinalStone Finance
title: CardinalStone Finance — Nomba cross-border payments debt facility, 2026
description: "Nomba, a Nigerian fintech that enables businesses to collect payments and access banking services, has raised a $3 million debt facility through CardinalStone Finance Company Limited, the financing arm of CardinalStone Group, to expand its cross-border payments infrastructure across Central Africa. The company said the debt facility will give it more USD liquidity to deploy through its banking relationships in Hong Kong and Singapore. With more liquidity available across currencies, the company can support more transactions and settle payments to deepen existing trade corridors and expand into new ones."
scope_basis: Debt facility for a fintech's cross-border payments infrastructure.

financier: Startup Abuja
title: Startup Abuja — Student Aid Programme, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source (French):

> L'organisation Startup Abuja ouvre les candidatures pour son programme d'aide destiné aux étudiants de l'enseignement supérieur au Nigeria. Dotée de 50 millions de nairas, soit plus de 37 000 dollars, cette initiative offre une prise en charge des frais de scolarité, une allocation mensuelle et des stages rémunérés à distance. L'objectif est d'apporter un soutien financier aux jeunes tout en leur enseignant les compétences pratiques de l'entrepreneuriat pour réussir leur insertion professionnelle.
scope_basis: Student aid covering tuition, stipends and internships; no digital activity is stated.

financier: EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
title: Nigeria Sovereign Fibre Project (Project BRIDGE)
description: Provision of a sovereign loan of up to USD 100 million to the Federal Republic of Nigeria to finance its participation in a special purpose vehicle (SPV) for the nationwide rollout of approximately 90,000 km of fibre-optic broadband infrastructure. The project supports Nigeria's National Broadband Plan, targeting connectivity for 50% of 33 million unserved Nigerians and raising fixed broadband penetration. SPV will operate as open-access wholesale provider. Co-financed in parallel by World Bank (USD 500m) and AfDB (USD 200m). Supported by EUR 22m EU grant for technical designs and capacity building for 2,000 technicians.
scope_basis: Sovereign loan funds Nigeria's stake in a company rolling out national fibre-optic broadband.

financier: European Union
title: European Union — Nigeria digitalisation (Global Gateway), 2026
description: "The European Union (EU), on Monday, announced a new investment package of EUR 290 million to be immediately mobilised in seven new operations in digitalisation, health and agricultural value chains... in the framework of the EU Global Gateway strategy." "The package of investments includes an additional EUR 131 million in the digitalisation sector, which will support the upgrade of digital connectivity and enhance digital services and skills." "Together with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the EU will contribute to the roll-out of 90,000 km of fiber optic cable across the country." "The EU will help develop secure and interoperable digital public infrastructure and data exchange systems for digital services to citizens and in the framework of Nigeria's 3 million Technical Talent programme."
scope_basis: The amount is the digitalisation share of the package: fibre, digital public infrastructure, digital services and skills.

financier: Gates Foundation
title: Gates Foundation and MTN Group Foundation — Nigeria Maternal Health Multiplier, 2026
description: "MTN Group Foundation (MTN) and the Gates Foundation announced a strategic partnership to launch the Nigeria Maternal Health Multiplier, a first-of-its-kind initiative in Nigeria to improve maternal health outcomes through an integrated digital ecosystem that connects women, frontline health workers, and primary health care facilities." "It will expand equitable access to high-quality maternal health care through three components: AI-enabled, phone-based decision support tools for both frontline health workers and mothers, affordable smartphones and mobile data, and improved connectivity at health care facilities." "The four-year partnership was announced at Semafor's Next 3 Billion event, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. It begins with an initial investment of approximately US$25 million between 2026 and 2030, including direct and in-kind contributions from the Gates Foundation and MTN. This anchor investment is intended to catalyze additional funding and support future expansion into other markets over time." Targets: "By 2030, the initiative aims to help 500,000 women access trusted health guidance, equip 5,000 frontline health workers with tools to identify complications from pregnancy and childbirth early, and enable 500 health facilities to deliver more consistent, higher-quality maternal health care."
scope_basis: All three components are digital: AI decision tools, smartphones and data, and facility connectivity.

financier: Norleo Space Investments
title: Terra Industries — Seed Round Close, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> Terra Industries, a Nigerian defence-technology startup that builds autonomous security systems using its proprietary software, has raised an additional $18 million, closing Africa's largest seed round at $52 million.
>
> Norleo Space Investments and angel investor Grant Gordon participated in the round as new investors alongside existing investors 8VC, Silent Ventures, Nova Global, Belief Capital, and SV Angel.
>
> Terra said in a statement that it will use the capital to open its first international office in London, expand its manufacturing capacity, accelerate deployment of its products across the Global South, and grow its team in the engineering, operations, and business development departments.
scope_basis: Seed equity in a technology start-up building software-driven autonomous systems.

financier: Village Capital
title: Village Capital — Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility, first Nigeria investments, 2026
description: "Village Capital, a global nonprofit that backs high-impact startups, has deployed $450,000 from its Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility into two Nigerian startups, marking the investment vehicle's entry into the country after backing two Ghanaian companies earlier this year. The backed companies include Trade Lenda, a digital financial services platform for small and medium-sized businesses, and AirSmat, a climate-tech company that turns agricultural waste into biochar-based fertiliser. The latest investments bring the facility's total portfolio to seven startups across Ghana and Nigeria. Village Capital launched the $4 million facility in July 2025 with backing from the Dutch Entrepreneurial Development Bank (FMO) and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO)."
scope_basis: Two start-ups funded; one is a digital finance platform, the other makes biochar fertiliser.

financier: Global Environment Facility (GEF)
title: Global Environment Facility — Senegal, climate transparency data platform (CBIT-Sénégal), 2025
description:
From the project document, verbatim:

> Senegal has insufficient capacity to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) of
> Article 13 of the Paris Agreement (PA) due to restricted exposure to previous transparency
> initiatives.

> This project objective is to enhance the National Framework for Climate Transparency for
> Senegal to meet the requirements of the ETF under the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. The
> project aims to fill critical information gaps, align with sustainable development goals,
> including gender equality and foster transparency and good governance, enabling Senegal to
> manage climate-related data and more effectively prepare fully transparent reports to the
> United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

> By improving the climate data management cycle—from planning and data collection to analysis
> and information sharing— Senegal will produce high-quality climate information for
> international reporting and national decision-making.

Three technical components: an **Integrated National Transparency Platform (NTP)** with the
governance frameworks, data flows, expertise and tools around it; **NTP modules** for the GHG
inventory, adaptation/vulnerability, NDC tracking, support needed and received, and
capacity-building needs; and **incorporation of the NTP into UNFCCC reporting and national
planning processes** via a roadmap, protocols and tools. Expected to benefit **120 individuals,
40% of them women**.
scope_basis: All components build a national climate transparency data platform and its modules.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: Chad - Support Program to Improve the Business Climate and the Modernization of Public Administration (PAACAMA)–Phase I
description: The Support Programme to Improve the Business Climate and Modernize Public Administration – Phase I (PAACAMA I) is a nationwide institutional support programme in Chad designed to strengthen public administration performance, improve domestic resource mobilization and make the economy more attractive to private investment. The programme will support the digitalization and interoperability of tax, customs, treasury and public finance systems; the modernization of tax-payment methods; the establishment of tax teleservice centres in N’Djamena and the provinces; and the strengthening of the external oversight of public finances through support to the Court of Accounts. It will also modernize and interconnect business-development and investment-promotion one-stop shops, establish digital services for special economic zones, improve the legal framework for investment, promote territorial marketing and facilitate the formalization and development of SMEs. The programme comprises three components: (i) support for domestic resource mobilization and stronger external oversight of public finances, (ii) support for improving the business climate, and (iii) programme coordination and management. Activities include upgrading the e-Tax, standardized electronic invoicing and SYDONIA systems; deploying electronic payment terminals and digital platforms; strengthening the National Investment and Exports Agency and the Agency for the Administration of Special Economic Zones; expanding regional business-support services; and supporting incubators, start-ups and young entrepreneurs, particularly in climate-resilient agro-processing, digital technologies and renewable energy. The total programme cost is estimated at UA 10.535 million, equivalent to approximately CFAF 8 billion. It will be financed by an African Development Fund grant of UA 9.52 million, representing 90% of the total cost, and an in-kind Government of Chad contribution of UA 1.015 million, equivalent to about CFAF 724 million. No external co-financing or trust-fund financing is included in the financing plan for this phase. The executing agency is the Ministry of Finance, Budget, Economy, Planning and International Cooperation, through the existing project implementation unit of the Economic Governance and Extractive Sector Support Project. scope_basis: Digital tax and customs systems sit beside audit court support, investment law reform, territorial marketing and SME formalisation.

financier: BGK
title: BGK — Cyber Defense Africa, 2026
description:
"BGK podpisał umowę określającą warunki udzielenia długoterminowego finansowania, zabezpieczonego m.in. gwarancją EFSD+ z unijnego Programu Transformacji Cyfrowej w Afryce Subsaharyjskiej. Planowana transakcja, o wartości ponad 100 mln zł, dotyczy polskiej inwestycji technologicznej w Togo. To pierwsze finansowanie BGK w formule współpracy rozwojowej."

"Projekt inwestycyjny, który częściowo sfinansuje BGK, realizuje Cyber Defense Africa (CDA). To spółka utworzona przez rząd Republiki Togo i polską firmę Asseco Data Systems w 2019 roku. [...] Projekt będzie realizowany przez 12 lat, a jego budżet przekracza 80 mln euro. BGK sfinansuje początkowy etap inwestycji kwotą ok. 24 mln euro, tj. ponad 100 mln zł. Środki są zabezpieczone unijną gwarancją z programu EFSD+."
scope_basis: Loan finances a cybersecurity company's investment project.

financier: Luxembourg Development Cooperation
title: Luxembourg — Togo digital-transformation and cybersecurity cooperation, 2026
description: "Le Togo et le Luxembourg [...] ont signé, le mercredi 16 juillet à Lomé, trois accords assortis d'un financement de 78,55 millions EUR (environ 90 millions USD). Une partie de cet engagement soutiendra la transformation numérique de l'administration togolaise et renforcera la sécurité des infrastructures numériques, notamment à travers le programme TogoCyber+." "Le nouveau Programme indicatif de coopération (PIC) 2026-2031 prévoit notamment un volet consacré à la transformation numérique, tandis que TogoCyber+ doit contribuer au renforcement des capacités nationales en matière de cybersécurité et de résilience numérique."
scope_basis: Amount covers three cooperation agreements; only part supports digital administration and cybersecurity, the rest being the wider cooperation programme.

financier: World Bank
title: World Bank — Togo WURI digital-ID additional financing, 2026
description: "Togo and the World Bank Group signed five financing agreements worth a combined $429 million, or about 257.4 billion CFA francs, in Lomé on Thursday, July 16, 2026." "Under the 'Unite' pillar, the West Africa Unique Identification for Regional Integration and Inclusion Project, known as WURI, will receive an additional $20 million to expand access to secure identification." The other agreements — PRIME-GAS ($40m) and WA-REMP ($100m) energy, COSO social cohesion ($69m) and PASLT logistics ($200m) — fall outside data governance / digital transformation.
scope_basis: Additional financing for a digital identification project.

financier: EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
title: EBRD — Tunisie Telecom (Project Hannibal), 2024
description: EBRD Board report (approved 24 July 2024) for Project Hannibal — "a development-linked loan to the Company in the amount of up to EUR 190 million, in four tranches, including a first committed tranche of EUR 50 million." The EBRD Loan is supported by a first-loss EU EFSD+ Digital Transformation guarantee and complemented by an EUR 11 million EU grant. It finances Tunisie Telecom's capital expenditure — connecting households to fibre, upgrading the fibre backbone, transitioning 3G to 4G and 4G+/5G, and participation in the pan-European MEDUSA submarine cable. Tunisie Telecom is 65% state-owned, 35% owned by Emirates International Telecommunications; the operation is the Bank's first Tunisian public-sector project without a sovereign guarantee.
scope_basis: Loan for a telecom operator's fibre, mobile network and submarine cable capital expenditure.

financier: Economic Development Cooperation Fund
title: Korea EDCF — Tanzania AI and digital technology training institute, 2026
description:
The ministry's own sentences, in the Korean it published in:

> 재정경제부는 제159차 대외경제협력기금(EDCF) 운용위원회(위원장: 재정경제부 장관)를 서면 개최하고, 탄자니아 AI‧디지털 기술교육기관 건립 사업 승인안과 EDCF 운용관리규정 개정안 등을 의결하였다.

> 탄자니아 AI‧디지털 기술교육기관 건립 사업은 탄자니아의 AI·디지털 산업 인력 양성을 위해 AI, 로보틱스, 데이터분석, IoT 등 4개 학과를 운영하는 첨단 기술교육기관을 건립하는 사업으로, 1.7억불 규모의 EDCF 차관이 지원될 예정이다.

> 동 사업은 교육시설과 캠퍼스 건축, AI Lab‧IoT‧로보틱스‧드론‧3D 프린터 등 AI 교육·실습 기자재 구축, ICT 및 네트워크 시스템 구축 및 교육과정 개발과 운영(O&M) 지원 등으로 구성된다.

> 동 사업은 우리 기업만 수주할 수 있는 ‘구속성(tied)’ 차관 사업으로, 금번 EDCF 차관 지원을 통해 AI, 에듀테크, 건설 등과 관련된 우리 기업의 아프리카 시장 진출 기회가 마련될 것으로 기대된다.

Scope, from those sentences and stated here in English as CC's reading rather than the ministry's words: an advanced technical training institute running four departments — AI, robotics, data analytics and IoT — comprising teaching facilities and campus construction, AI teaching and practical equipment (AI Lab, IoT, robotics, drones, 3D printers), a high-performance AI training facility built around AI compute, HBM and high-speed networking, ICT and network systems, curriculum development, and operations and maintenance support. The loan is tied: only Korean firms may win the contracts.
scope_basis: Loan builds and equips an institute dedicated to AI, robotics, data analytics and IoT training.

financier: U.S. Department of State
recipient: Government of Uganda / Ministry of Health
title: U.S. Department of State — Uganda health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
"2.5.3 Funding Plan: The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $26,129,831; 2027 $24,779,640; 2028 $25,103,354; 2029 $27,294,065; 2030 $9,795,399. TOTAL $113,102,289."

Uganda controls what the money builds: it "plans to determine and approve the national data and health information architecture prior to any investment financed under this MOU", the US "plans to fund data systems investments within the budget reflected in Section 2.5.3 on projects as determined jointly by both Participants", and "All data generated through U.S.-funded programs is expected to be owned by the Government of Uganda" (2.5.2).

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$1,719,960,000 against Uganda's US$577,001,796 (Appendix 1). Non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement" (6.9), every figure "subject to the availability of funds".
scope_basis: The amount is the MOU's dedicated funding line for health data systems.

description: UNICEF has submitted an application to Sida for multi­year funding (2025–2027) for a new initiative run by UNICEF's Innovation Hub in Stockholm. The aim is to provide support to the female health tech industry in Africa, commonly known as FemTech. The initiative will be run by UNICEF's Innovation Hub in Stockholm and the so­called Venture Fund. UNICEF is applying for SEK 45 000 000 for 2025­2027. The female health technology industry, focuses on leveraging technology to address women's health and wellbeing needs. In recent years, the FemTech industry has seen impressive growth encompassing technologies aimed at enhancing women and girl’s sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) with products, services, and solutions predominantly built for, by, and with women and girls. While there has been a notable growth in Femtech founders and solutions across the industry, limited attention has been paid to founder talent in emerging markets and designing solutions that solve the diverse health needs of women and girls in low and middle income countries. The objective of this new initiative is to: ­Increase awareness and access to, and respect for, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for all, to empower girls and young women ­Improve the availability and quality of healthcare products and services for girls and women; ­Increase investment flows to these solutions

financier: International Development Research Centre
recipient: Institute of Policy Research and Analysis (Uganda)
title: African Growth and AI Network: IPRA
description:
The African Growth and AI Network (AGAIN) will generate context-specific evidence on how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour markets, productivity and inequality as adoption of AI accelerates. This project will coordinate data collection and analysis across multiple African countries to inform inclusive AI policies that support decent work and economic resilience. The Institute of Policy Research and Analysis (IPRA) in Uganda will collect harmonized data from 1,200 firms and 4,500 workers in Uganda, Kenya and South Africa, analyze large-scale job posting data and link findings, where possible, to tax and social protection records. The project will also test practical policy responses through a worker support experiment and a regulatory sandbox for digital labour platforms.

Key outcomes include open datasets, country-level policy papers and practical tools to support fair and inclusive AI governance.

AGAIN is part of Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D), a partnership between IDRC and the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. It aims to strengthen policy, innovation and leadership for responsible and inclusive AI development in Africa.
scope_basis: Research project on AI's effects, producing open datasets and AI policy tools.

"The African Continental Free Trade Area Secretariat has signed a 20-year, $3.1 billion concession agreement with Bergmans Security Consultants and Supplies Limited to modernise customs administration across Africa in a move aimed at accelerating intra-African trade, reducing border bottlenecks and improving revenue collection."

"The agreement, signed in Abuja on Thursday, will drive the implementation of the AfCFTA Customs Modernisation Project, an initiative designed to deploy advanced digital technologies and customs infrastructure to support the continent's free trade agenda."

"He said Bergmans would finance the entire $3.1 billion project under the concession agreement and deploy digital and physical customs infrastructure across the continent to modernise border operations, improve trade corridors and simplify cross-border movement of goods."

"According to him, the project would introduce advanced non-intrusive inspection technology, integrated data centres and multilingual customs portals capable of supporting Africa's official languages."

Mene said the project "would provide the digital infrastructure needed to implement AfCFTA protocols on customs harmonisation and trade facilitation, enabling customs administrations across the continent to improve efficiency, strengthen revenue collection and facilitate the seamless movement of goods without imposing additional financial obligations on member states."
scope_basis: Customs modernisation concession covering physical border infrastructure and inspection equipment as well as data centres and customs portals.
