title: Cassava Technologies — DFC $50M Strategic Equity Investment
description: DFC direct equity investment of $50 million in Cassava Technologies Ltd., one of Africa's largest pan-African digital infrastructure and services platforms. Cassava operates over 110,000 km of fibre optic networks across 30 countries, data centres, cloud services, cybersecurity, and AI tools. DFC led the equity round alongside Google LLC and Finnfund. Investment supports data centre expansion in Kenya, Ghana, Nigeria (and Morocco), providing directed use of proceeds for new data centre construction. Counters risks from strategic competitor digital ecosystems. Cassava equity round total $90M.
scope_basis: Equity in a digital infrastructure group, directed at new data centre construction.

financier: e&
title: Moov Africa SSA Subsidiaries Annual CapEx 2024 - Network and Licence Investment
description: Maroc Telecom's capital expenditures in its sub-Saharan African subsidiaries operating under the Moov Africa brand reached MAD 7.96 billion ($800 million) in 2024, up 75.6% from MAD 4.54 billion in 2023. Of the total, MAD 3.549 billion was for frequency and licence acquisitions. Subsidiaries covered: Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Benin, Togo, Niger, Gabon, Mauritania, Mali, Chad, Central African Republic. e& (Etisalat Group) owns 53% of Maroc Telecom which in turn owns these subsidiaries.
scope_basis: Mobile operators' capital expenditure on networks and spectrum licences; the whole business is telecoms.

financier: European Investment Bank (EIB)
title: AXIAN TELECOM EXPANSION (MADAGASCAR AND TANZANIA)
description: Financing package to AXIAN Telecom to expand 4G mobile broadband network infrastructure across Madagascar and Tanzania, and introduction of 5G coverage. Global Gateway investment backed by EU budgetary guarantee. USD 60M for Tanzania, USD 40M for Madagascar. Supports inclusive digitalisation and sustainable development.
scope_basis: Financing for a telecom operator's 4G and 5G network expansion.

financier: Finnfund
title: Cassava Technologies Pan-African Digital Infrastructure Equity
description: Finnfund participated in a USD 90 million equity investment in Cassava Technologies alongside DFC and Google. Cassava is a pan-African ICT platform operating Liquid Intelligent Technologies (fibre), Africa Data Centres, Liquid C2 (cloud), Cassava.ai (AI), and Sasai Fintech across multiple SSA countries. Investment supports digital infrastructure expansion and connectivity for millions across the continent.
scope_basis: Equity in a group whose businesses are fibre, data centres, cloud, AI and fintech.

financier: FMO
title: TIDE Africa II SSA Early-Stage Tech VC Fund (TLcom Capital)
description: FMO Ventures Program USD 10M commitment to TIDE Africa II LP, TLcom Capital's second Africa-focused VC fund. Invests in early-stage tech and tech-enabled companies at Seed and Series A in East and West Africa. Fund closed at USD 154M.
scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund for early-stage tech companies.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: Airtel Africa High-Speed Mobile Connectivity Expansion II (2024)
description: IFC committed $165 million from its own account plus $35 million from the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) — a total of $200 million — to Airtel Africa to support expansion of high-speed mobile connectivity in DRC, Kenya, and Rwanda. Announced September 2024, the financing supports network upgrades including 4G and 5G-ready infrastructure and aims to improve access to high-speed internet for underserved populations across three key markets. This is IFC's second major Airtel Africa financing round, following the $194M package in 2022.
scope_basis: Loan to a mobile operator for 4G and 5G-ready network expansion.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: WIOCC Group Sustainability-Linked Debt Facility (2024)
description: IFC provided a sustainability-linked debt package to WIOCC Group comprising a $10 million USD loan and a ZAR 200 million (~$10.9 million) loan. Proparco co-financed $20 million and RMB provided an additional $10 million. Total package approximately $50 million. The financing expands WIOCC's core and edge data centres in DRC, Nigeria, and South Africa and grows its fibre networks. Sustainability-linked structure ties pricing to WIOCC's commitment to improve data centre energy efficiency and obtain EDGE green building certification, linking digital infrastructure investment with sustainability performance.
scope_basis: Debt funds a carrier's data centres and fibre networks.

financier: Mastercard
title: Mastercard $200M Minority Stake in MTN Group Fintech
description: Mastercard finalized a definitive agreement with MTN Group on February 5, 2024 to acquire a minority stake of up to $200 million in MTN Group Fintech, valuing the business at $5.2 billion. MTN Group Fintech encompasses MTN Mobile Money (MoMo), with 60 million active monthly wallets. The partnership spans 13 African markets and includes: launching a virtual/physical Mastercard companion card for MoMo wallets, expanding merchant acceptance via SME-in-a-Box, cross-border remittances, and cybersecurity solutions across Mastercard's network.
scope_basis: Equity stake in a mobile money and fintech business.

financier: Orange
title: Sonatel Group Annual CapEx 2024 - 5G Launch, Fibre and Mobile Network Expansion
description: Sonatel Group invested approximately XOF 300 billion in 2024 (representing 17% of turnover of XOF 1,776.4 billion) across Senegal, Mali, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, and Sierra Leone. Investments included 5G launch in Senegal, extension of fibre optic network, mobile broadband coverage expansion (4G reaching 98% of Senegal population), and satellite internet launch.
scope_basis: Telecom operator capex on 5G, fibre, mobile broadband coverage and satellite internet.

financier: Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
title: Africell USD 300M Bond - EAIF Sole Impact Investor
description: EAIF acted as sole impact investor anchoring Africell's debut USD 300 million international public bond (oversubscribed at $550M+). The financing supports roll-out of digital infrastructure across Angola, DRC, Gambia and Sierra Leone, enhancing connectivity for Africell's 14 million+ customers. EAIF committed USD 28 million (sole DFI/impact investor in the bond).
scope_basis: Bond investment in a mobile operator rolling out digital infrastructure.

financier: Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
title: IHS Towers Bond - EAIF Co-Anchor Investment
description: EAIF acted as co-anchor investor alongside IFC and Proparco in IHS Holding Limited's USD 1.2 billion bond issuance (oversubscribed at $2.3B). Proceeds refinance existing debt and support organic growth in African subsidiaries operating in Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, and Zambia. IHS Towers is a leading independent telecom tower company with over 40,000 towers in Africa.
scope_basis: Bond investment in a telecom tower company.

financier: Proparco
title: Africell Holding Limited — USD 300 Million Bond (Mobile Network Operator SSA)
description: DFI participation in Africell Holding Limited's debut USD 300 million public senior secured bond (10.5% coupon, due 2029). Africell operates mobile networks in DRC, Sierra Leone, Uganda, and Gambia. Bond proceeds refinanced existing capital structure and fund network expansion. EAIF participated as sole impact investor (USD 28M). Proparco and IFC also participated as DFI anchor investors. Proparco's specific allocation not publicly disclosed.
scope_basis: Bond participation in a mobile network operator.

financier: Proparco
title: IHS Holding Limited — USD 1.2 Billion Bond (Anchor Investor, Broadband Tower Infrastructure)
description: USD 20 million participation as anchor investor (with IFC and EAIF) in IHS Holding Limited's oversubscribed USD 1.2 billion dual-tranche senior notes issuance. IHS Towers is one of the world's largest independent tower companies with major presence in Nigeria, Zambia, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, Rwanda. Bond catalysed private investment (10x+ mobilisation). Supports digital connectivity across Africa.
scope_basis: Bond participation in a telecom tower company.

financier: Proparco
recipient: WIOCC Group / Open Access Data Centres (OADC)
title: WIOCC Group / Open Access Data Centres (OADC) — Data Centre Expansion DRC, Nigeria, South Africa
description: USD 20 million sustainability-linked loan to WIOCC Group (via its subsidiary Open Access Data Centres / OADC) to finance expansion of core and edge data centres in the DRC, Nigeria, and South Africa. Pricing linked to energy efficiency improvements and EDGE green building certification. Co-financed with IFC (USD 10M + ZAR 200M) and RMB. Total package USD 41M.
scope_basis: Loan to expand core and edge data centres.

financier: SIFEM
recipient: Apis Growth Markets Fund III (AGMF III)
title: Apis Growth Markets Fund III — SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed USD 20 million to Apis Growth Markets Fund III, a USD 500 million closed-end financial services fund targeting growth-stage opportunities in Africa, South Asia and Southeast Asia. The fund invests in transformative tech-enabled financial services including cashless payments, embedded finance and digital lending, enabling underserved populations to participate in the formal economy.
scope_basis: Fund investing in tech-enabled financial services such as cashless payments and digital lending.

financier: SIFEM
title: Helios Investors Fund V — SIFEM Digital Infrastructure and Financial Services
description: SIFEM committed USD 15 million to Helios Investors Fund V, a pan-African growth equity fund targeting mid-market companies benefiting from Africa's demographic expansion and urbanisation. The fund focuses on digital infrastructure, financial services, and tech-enabled business services, with a 50% gender equality commitment for portfolio companies.
scope_basis: Growth equity fund; financial services and business services sit alongside digital infrastructure.

financier: UK FCDO
title: Unlocking Digital Impact for Development (UDID) — Digital Development Activities Phase 2
description: Continuation phase of the FCDO-DIAL partnership for digital development activities, launched September 2025. Supports ongoing digital public goods ecosystem development, digital transformation advisory, and open-source solutions for development challenges. Maintains FCDO engagement with the Digital Impact Alliance for dissemination of digital development principles and supporting DPI adoption in low- and middle-income countries, with Africa as a primary region of focus.
scope_basis: Programme supports digital public goods and digital transformation advisory.

financier: UK FCDO
recipient: FCDO and partner organisations (innovation and experimentation)
title: Frontier Technologies — Testing New Solutions for Global Development and Diplomacy
description: Supports innovation and experimentation with frontier technologies to improve welfare and livelihoods of people in developing countries. Enables FCDO staff and partners to test new technology solutions to development challenges, strengthen adoption of effective innovations, and build local capacity. Activities include piloting new ideas, supporting integration of technologies (including AI and digital tools) into existing FCDO programmes, and generating evidence on what works in frontier technology for development.
scope_basis: Programme tests frontier technologies, including AI and digital tools, in development work.

financier: Global Affairs Canada
title: Bridging the Digital Gender Gap in Cameroon and Senegal
description: Strengthens economic empowerment and resilience of women through increased participation in digital economy in Cameroon and Senegal. Supports digital skills, access to technology, and women-led digital enterprises.
scope_basis: Project supports women's digital skills, access to technology and digital enterprises.

financier: Gates Foundation
recipient: International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore (IIITB)
title: Modular Open Source Identification Platform (MOSIP) Phase 3
description: To support inclusive digital identity systems by expanding global access to secure, open-source technology that enables governments to deliver trusted, privacy-preserving services to underserved populations.
scope_basis: Grant supports an open-source digital identity platform.

financier: Gates Foundation
title: Evidence on Digital Cash Transfers on Women's Nutrition and Health
description: To generate evidence on the role of digital in enhancing unrestricted cash transfers for women and children's nutrition and health outcomes.
scope_basis: Research on the role of digital delivery in cash transfers; no other use is named.

financier: Gates Foundation
title: Tax Administration Technology Innovation Hub
description: To support the Tax Administration Technology Innovation Hub and strengthen tobacco and health taxation in Africa
scope_basis: Supports a tax technology innovation hub and also tobacco and health taxation work.

financier: Gates Foundation
title: South Africa Group of Twenty & Digital Public Infrastructure Roadmap
description: To provide technical support through partners to the South African government in developing Digital Public Infrastructure to provide vulnerable populations with improved access to better services.
scope_basis: Technical support for a digital public infrastructure roadmap.

financier: Sida
title: GSMA 2025-2028 (Connectivity in LMICs)
description: Sida core grant to GSMA for connectivity and digital inclusion in LMICs 2025-2028. The programme supports mobile broadband expansion, internet access and digital ecosystem development across sub-Saharan Africa and other regions.
scope_basis: Core grant for mobile broadband expansion and digital inclusion.

financier: Cassava Technologies
title: Cassava Technologies — NVIDIA AI factory, Africa's first: US$720m programme announced 2025
description: Cassava Technologies announced on 24 March 2025 that it plans to build Africa's first AI factory — a data-centre facility powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deployed using NVIDIA Cloud Partner reference architectures. Strive Masiyiwa, founder and chairman, framed it as infrastructure for the AI economy that keeps data within Africa's borders; Jaap Zuiderveld, NVIDIA VP EMEA, confirmed the NCP partnership. Cassava committed to deploy at its South African data centres **by June 2025**, with expansion planned to its facilities in **Egypt, Kenya, Morocco and Nigeria**. On 7 April 2025 Bloomberg reported the programme's cost at **US$720 million**, covering roughly 12,000 NVIDIA GPUs across five regional hubs over three to four years. The South Africa hub went live in November 2025. In October 2025 NVIDIA took an equity stake in Cassava (amount undisclosed) as part of a US$150m+ equity raise for Liquid Intelligent Technologies, and STANLIB agreed a minority stake in Africa Data Centres. Primary sub-Saharan countries are ZAF, NGA and KEN; Egypt and Morocco are outside SSA.
scope_basis: GPU-equipped data-centre capacity for AI across five hubs.

financier: British International Investment
recipient: Axian Telecom Holding and Management plc
title: Axian Telecom Holding — Debt Investment (2025)
description: Third BII debt investment in Axian Telecom Holding and Management plc (parent entity), committed June 2025. Axian Telecom is a pan-African telecommunications and digital infrastructure company operating across multiple African markets including Madagascar, Tanzania, Togo, Senegal, Comoros, and Réunion, providing mobile services, broadband connectivity, and mobile financial services.
scope_basis: Debt investment in a telecom group providing mobile, broadband and mobile financial services.

financier: DEG
title: DEG Anchor Investment in AXIAN Telecom USD 600M Bond (2025)
description: DEG participates as anchor investor in the USD 600 million 7.250% senior notes due 2030 issued by AXIAN Telecom. The bond is part of a USD 160 million anchor investment by five development finance institutions: EAIF (USD 40M), IFC, BII, DEG, and Proparco (USD 25M). The bond was oversubscribed 2x with over USD 1.3 billion in demand. AXIAN Telecom operates across nine African markets including Madagascar, Senegal, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, DRC, and Comoros. Proceeds used to refinance existing debt and invest in digital infrastructure, smartphone access, and mobile financial services to expand digital inclusion across Africa.
scope_basis: Bond issued by a telecoms group for refinancing and digital infrastructure.

financier: Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
title: EAIF — Axian Telecom USD 600m bond anchor, 2025
description:
Verbatim from the financier's own release:

> London, 21 July: The Emerging Africa & Asia Infrastructure Fund (EAAIF), a Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) company managed by Ninety One, today announced its anchor investment in Axian Telecom’s USD 600 million 5-year bond issuance. EAAIF invested USD 40 million as part of a USD 160 million anchor investment alongside the International Finance Corporation (IFC), British International Investment (BII), DEG, and Proparco.

> EAAIF’s investment will support, among other key initiatives, Axian Telecom’s capital expenditure across its subsidiaries – driving economic growth and providing improved digital infrastructure to millions of people.
scope_basis: Bond investment in a telecoms group for network capital expenditure.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
recipient: Maroc Telecom, for its subsidiaries Moov Africa Chad and Moov Africa Malitel (TCD, MLI)
title: IFC — Maroc Telecom (Moov Africa Chad and Moov Africa Malitel), 4G rollout, 2025
description: "Morocco-based Maroc Telecom announced on Saturday it has secured two loans from World Bank Group's IFC worth EUR370 million (US$425.1 million) to help finance 4G rollouts in Chad and Mali." "Maroc Telecom said the loans will enable its subsidiary operators in those countries – Moov Africa Chad and Moov Africa Malitel – to roll out 4G services, bringing faster, more reliable internet to more people and businesses across both countries. The telco didn't specify how the loans would be split between Chad and Mali."
scope_basis: Loans to finance 4G rollout by two mobile operators.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: Raxio Data Centres — IFC Debt Facility ($100M, 2025)
description: IFC committed $100 million to Raxio Group to develop a leading Sub-Saharan African data centre platform. The financing comprises $60 million senior debt and $40 million subordinated debt. Raxio operates carrier-neutral Tier III data centres in Ethiopia, Mozambique, DRC, Côte d'Ivoire, Tanzania, Angola, and Uganda, addressing the critical shortage of colocation and cloud infrastructure across the continent. The investment enables Raxio to accelerate construction of new data centres and expand capacity in existing facilities, supporting digital transformation across multiple SSA markets.
scope_basis: Debt for a data centre operator to build and expand facilities.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: IFC — WIOCC Group sustainability-linked loan (WIOCC VI Debt), 2025
description:
Verbatim from IFC's Environmental & Social Review Summary for project 51154:

> IFC’s proposed financing package includes an equity investment of up to US$50 million and a sustainability-linked loan of up to US$20.4 million equivalent (a US$10 million tranche and a South African Rand tranche of US$10.4 million equivalent). The project’s principal activities include: (a) acquiring capacity from existing submarine cables, (b) expanding data centre infrastructure, (c) growing the new fiber-to-the-home/business (FTTx), and (d) investing in terrestrial fibre. Key efforts are focused on increasing data centre capacity in South Africa and Nigeria through the construction of a new block at the Lagos (Lekki) Data Centre and the expansion of the current facility in Durban.

Verbatim from IFC's Summary of Investment Information for the same project:

> The proposed IFC investment comprises a senior secured sustainability-linked loan (“SLF”) of up to US$20.8 mn to WIOCC’s subsidiaries: WIOCC Mauritius (“WIOCC MU”) (US$ loan) and OADC PropCo South Africa (“OADC SA”) (ZAR loan), jointly referred to as “WIOCC Group”.

> This current project is considered an extension of WIOCC SLF loan (#48053) and OADC SLF Loan (#49887) which also sought to enhance connectivity and data hosting services for individuals and businesses in Africa.

Project events as disclosed by IFC: Approved 5 December 2025; Signed 10 December 2025; Invested 14 May 2026.
scope_basis: Loan funds submarine capacity, data centres and fibre.

financier: Norfund
title: CREI Solar Energy for Telecom Towers — Mali, South Sudan, Central African Republic
description: Norfund USD 30 million debt investment in CREI, backed by Cygnum Capital's Facility for Energy Inclusion (FEI). Total package USD 90 million (FEI USD 60M + Norfund USD 30M), refinancing USD 55M bridge facilities provided in 2024 plus USD 35M new capital. Modernises approximately 4,000 telecom tower sites in Mali, South Sudan, and Central African Republic with solar energy, enabling mobile connectivity and broadband in fragile states.
scope_basis: Debt to a telecom tower infrastructure company for powering tower sites.

financier: Proparco
title: Axian Telecom Holding — USD 600 Million Bond (Digital Access Africa)
description: USD 25 million participation in Axian Telecom Holding's USD 600 million public bond issuance. Axian Telecom is a pan-African mobile network operator with operations in Madagascar, Tanzania, Togo, Senegal, Benin, and other SSA markets. Bond proceeds support network expansion, 4G/5G rollout, and digital connectivity across francophone and lusophone Africa.
scope_basis: Bond participation in a mobile network operator for network expansion.

financier: BMZ
title: Pan-African e-Commerce Initiative Panafrikanische E-Commerce Initiative
description: Context:   Electronic commerce, also known as e-commerce, has grown significantly during recent years to become an important procurement and sales channel in emerging African economies. The adoption of the Digital Trade Protocol of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) brought improvements in the regulatory framework. Now the protocol has to be implemented and the prerequisites put in place for African companies to participate in cross-border e-commerce. They include secure and afford
scope_basis: Initiative supports cross-border e-commerce.

financier: Africa Finance Corporation
recipient: Lightrock Africa Fund II / Future Africa Fund III
title: AFC Africa-Focused Technology Fund Managers Commitment
description: AFC's Board approved a commitment of up to USD 100 million to invest in Africa-focused technology fund managers, aiming to address the shortage of long-term institutional capital for African technology companies. Initial deployments: (i) USD 25 million anchor commitment to Lightrock Africa Fund II (Lightrock portfolio includes Moniepoint, Lula, M-KOPA); (ii) USD 15 million to Future Africa Fund III (early-stage venture capital backing technology-enabled solutions). The remaining USD 60 million is earmarked for additional fund managers under evaluation. Sectors covered: fintech, digital infrastructure, consumer technology, education technology. The commitment represents AFC's strategic entry into Africa's venture capital ecosystem to mobilise institutional capital and deepen African ownership of tech investment.
scope_basis: Commitment to fund managers investing in African technology companies.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: African Development Bank Group — Saviu II fund, 2026
description: "The African Development Bank Group is investing 6.5 million euro stake in the Saviu II fund to support technology start-ups in French-speaking Africa." "The Bank Group will invest 4.5 million euros as equity and 2 million euros as a first-loss hedging tranche on behalf of the European Commission, under the Boost Africa Programme." "The Saviu II venture capital fund aims to make at least 60% of its commitments in the French-speaking countries of West and Central Africa: Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Benin, Senegal, Togo, Burkina Faso and Mali." "Saviu II... plans to invest between 500,000 and three million euros in about 20 technology or technology-oriented B2B start-ups in the seed phase or carrying out first institutional fundraising."
scope_basis: Stake in a venture fund for technology start-ups.

financier: Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF)
title: EAIF — Liquid Intelligent Technologies pan-African fibre refinancing, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the financier's own release:

> EAAIF has also committed USD 50 million to Liquid Intelligent Technologies as part of a USD 450 million restructuring and expansion package. This investment supports the optimisation of Liquid's capital structure and the maintenance of its 110,000 km cross-border fibre network across 25 countries, including Kenya, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

> This network is key for Africa's digital data storage and processing, serving major operators, enterprises, and hyperscalers. By investing in Liquid's high-speed broadband and cloud infrastructure, EAAIF reinforces its commitment to sovereign digital assets that drive economic growth.

> EAAIF's green covenants also align with Liquid Intelligent Technologies' parent company, Cassava Technologies, in its transition path to achieve a 42% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030.
scope_basis: Loan to a fibre network operator for refinancing and network maintenance.

financier: EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
title: EBRD — Yas Kenya/Senegal network expansion, 2026
description:
"The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is providing a senior loan of up to €270 million to pan-African telecoms operator Yas to fund network expansion in Senegal and Kenya." "The deal marks the EBRD's first investment in Senegal and its first local-currency financing and A/B loan structure in sub-Saharan Africa." "The committed facility totals up to €170 million, split between a €100 million EBRD A-loan, a B-loan of up to €50 million to be syndicated to institutional investors, and a local-currency facility of up to €20 million equivalent in Kenyan shillings. Amsterdam-based impact private credit fund ILX Fund will take a sizeable position in the B-loan. A further uncommitted facility of up to €100 million is available for future Yas acquisitions and capital expenditure." "Yas, owned by AXIAN Telecom, will use the funding to expand 4G, 5G and fibre infrastructure across both markets." In Kenya the capital modernises the Zuku fibre network (Yas acquired Zuku's parent Wananchi Group in 2025).

Recipient countries: KEN, SEN.
scope_basis: Loan to a telecom operator to expand 4G, 5G and fibre networks.

financier: FinDev Canada
title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund II — SSA/Global Fintech Lending
description: FinDev Canada provides USD 15 million loan (including USD 7 million from 2X Canada blended finance facility) to Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund II, a 7-year global debt fund with USD 250 million target size. The fund deploys asset-backed capital to fintech platforms serving MSMEs and low-income consumers in Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia using data integration technology for credit risk monitoring and lending to digitally enabled, underserved segments.
scope_basis: Loan to a debt fund that lends to fintech platforms.

financier: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
title: IFC — Airtel Africa network expansion loan, 2026
description: "IFC's $150 million loan to two of Airtel Africa's subsidiaries will help the company expand and upgrade mobile networks over the coming years. In doing so, it will broaden access to high-speed data connectivity in underserved communities, enabling small businesses to grow, entrepreneurs to reach new markets and young people to access digital opportunities." IFC notes its support includes longer-tenor and local-currency financing.
scope_basis: Loan to mobile operator subsidiaries to expand and upgrade mobile networks.

financier: Proparco
recipient: Novastar Ventures / Africa People and Planet Fund III (NVIII)
title: Novastar Ventures Africa People and Planet Fund III — Seed-to-Growth Tech Fund SSA
description: USD 5 million commitment to Novastar Ventures Africa People and Planet Fund III (NVIII), a USD 147 million pan-African venture capital fund (final close 2026). Fund invests from seed to growth stage ($1M–$8M per company) in tech-enabled solutions combining economic growth with positive environmental impact. Sectors: delivery, e-mobility, smartphone access, sustainable agriculture. Part of Proparco's Choose Africa VC programme (EU/EFSD+).
scope_basis: Venture fund whose tech-enabled portfolio spans e-mobility and sustainable agriculture as well as digital businesses.

financier: Agence Française de Développement
recipient: UN Women; National Statistics Institutes (SN, TD, MR)
title: Gender Statistics Support — Senegal, Mauritania and Chad (Women Count Phase 2)
description: Phase 2 of Women Count programme. Improves production and use of gender-disaggregated data to track SDGs, women's economic empowerment, and gender-based violence. Modernises data systems in Senegal, Chad, and Mauritania; engages statistics institutes, ministries, women's organisations and media. Financed through UN Women.
scope_basis: Production and use of gender statistics through national statistics institutes.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: MULTINATIONAL - Support Project to improve Access to Financial Services for the Vulnerable Population Groups in the WAEMU Zone (PAASF - UEMOA)
description: The PAASF-UEMOA project (Projet d'Appui à l'Amélioration de l'Accès aux Services Financiers des Saisons Vulnérables dans la Zone UEMOA) complements the PRDEN in that it targets the financial inclusion of vulnerable groups, notably women, young people, startups, MSMEs and rural populations, by levera...
scope_basis: Financial inclusion project; the description is cut off before saying how far it relies on digital means.

financier: Gates Foundation
title: Digital Infrastructure Reforms for the overall economy in Africa- Phase 2
description: To make Digital Financial Inclusion reforms work for the overall economy in Africa by building unified country level coordinating mechanisms of all essential building blocks that serve the economy.
scope_basis: Supports digital financial inclusion reforms and their country coordination.

financier: European Union
title: European Union / Expertise France — Africa Connect Digital Campus, 2025
description: "Projet ... Publié le 12 mars 2026 ... Date de début du projet: 15 octobre 2025 ... En cours ... Date de fin du projet: 15 avril 2029 ... Montant (euro): 4,2 M ... Pays et région: Bénin, Côte d'Ivoire, Togo, Afrique." Sector tags on the project page: "Education, enseignement supérieur et recherche" and "Développement humain."
scope_basis: Text gives only dates, amount and education sector tags for a project titled digital campus.

financier: Gates Foundation
title: Strengthening the Agri payment value proposition
description: To test and scale digital payment services that help smallholder farmers and rural merchants increase income, resilience, and access to financial tools.
scope_basis: Grant tests and scales digital payment services for farmers and rural merchants.

financier: AfCFTA Adjustment Fund
recipient: Telecel Global Services Ltd, subsidiary of the Mauritius-based Telecel Group (GHA, LBR)
title: AfCFTA Adjustment Fund — Telecel Global Services, 2025
description: "The Credit Fund of the AfCFTA Adjustment Fund has successfully closed its first investment, committing US$10 million to Telecel Global Services Ltd, through a senior secured amortising loan." "With digital connectivity being at the heart of the trade and economic integration and success of the AfCFTA, this facility will support Telecel's expansion in Ghana and Liberia, strengthen its infrastructure, and contribute to bridging Africa's digital divide through enhanced connectivity and digital inclusion."
scope_basis: Loan to a telecoms company to expand connectivity infrastructure.

financier: African Development Bank (AfDB)
title: African Development Bank — WATAF Strengthening Tax Administration Capacity Project in West Africa (STACP-WA), 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> Liberia is among six West African countries set to benefit from a US$5.3 million African Development Bank (AfDB)-financed initiative designed to strengthen tax administration, improve domestic revenue mobilization, and build resilient revenue systems across the region.
>
> The four-year Strengthening Tax Administration Capacity Project in West Africa (STACP-WA) was officially launched by the West African Tax Administration Forum (WATAF) on Tuesday, August 18.
>
> The initiative is financed through a UA4 million grant from the African Development Fund/Transition Support Facility Pillar III, equivalent to approximately US$5.3 million. It will benefit Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.
>
> Bangura said the project will help beneficiary countries improve domestic, trade, and extractive-sector tax administration, strengthen compliance, and reduce revenue leakages.
>
> It will also support digital tax tools, VAT and e-invoicing reforms, taxpayer education, gender-responsive tax systems, and improved governance of natural resource revenues.
>
> According to Bangura, the project has three main components: strengthening the efficient administration of domestic and trade taxes; improving natural resource revenues in resource-rich countries; and supporting project management, coordination, and institutional capacity development within the WATAF Secretariat.
scope_basis: Tax administration capacity project; digital tax tools and e-invoicing sit beside natural resource revenue and taxpayer education work.

financier: European Commission
title: Regional Energy Governance and Information System for West Africa (REGIS WA)
description: To contribute to the overall objective, the project supports ECOWAS through two components. Component 1 supports implementation and monitoring/follow-up of the regional energy policy, transposition in Member States of the regional directives and the regional energy action plan, and liaison with the African Union. Component 2 supports the development of ECOWAS's energy statistical system — improving capacities and supporting Member States in the collection and production of statistical energy data, monitoring that collection and production, providing equipment, software and training at the level of ECOWAS and its Member States, strengthening collaboration with the African Energy Commission (AFREC, based in Algiers) on energy statistics, and integrating a gender-sensitive approach where possible.
scope_basis: The energy statistical system is one component; the other supports regional energy policy implementation.

RMB acted as Coordinator, Initial Mandated Lead Arranger, and Bookrunner. The financing enables ADC to accelerate expansion at its existing Midrand (JHB1) and Samrand (JHB2) Johannesburg campuses and Cape Town (CPT1/CPT2) facilities. ADC's South Africa market has capacity of 64MW and the expansion aims to increase this further to serve growing hyperscaler and enterprise demand.
scope_basis: Financing facility to expand hyperscale data centre capacity.

USD 355 million). Actis leads the consortium via Towerco Bidco with a 70% stake; Royal Bafokeng Holdings holds 30%. Swiftnet operates approximately 4,000 towers and masts across South Africa. Transaction completed March 2025 following regulatory approvals from Competition Tribunal (September 2024) and ICASA (December 2024).
scope_basis: Acquisition of a telecom masts and towers company, whose whole business is connectivity infrastructure.

TMWF provides affordable broadband connectivity to households and small businesses in areas typically excluded from fibre rollout. This investment directly supports digital inclusion and connectivity access.

financier: Ninety One
recipient: Open Access Data Centres (OADC), a WIOCC subsidiary
title: Ninety One — Open Access Data Centres local-currency loan for a new South African data centre, 2025
description:
Verbatim from the release:

> Ninety One also committed $15 million in local currency to Open Access Data Centres (OADC), a WIOCC subsidiary, to construct a new data centre in South Africa and expand existing facilities.

> The funding forms part of a total $65 million debt raise which includes a $20 million commitment from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and $15 million from Proparco.

> All financing arrangements, including EAAIF’s $15 million senior secured loan facility, have a 10-year tenor and are structured as sustainability-linked facilities. The cost of the financing is directly tied to WIOCC achieving ambitious sustainability-linked targets, ensuring that its digital expansion is also sustainable. Key performance indicators include EDGE certification for new data centres – a global standard for resource-efficient and zero-carbon buildings – and Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) targets for operating facilities.
scope_basis: Loan to build a new data centre and expand existing ones.

financier: DEG
recipient: Naked Insurance (Naked Financial Technology Pty Ltd)
title: DEG Equity Investment in Naked Insurtech South Africa Series B2 (2025)
description: DEG provides USD 4 million in equity capital to South African insurtech Naked Insurance as part of its USD 38 million Series B2 funding round. The round is led by global impact investor BlueOrchard with continued support from Hollard Insurance, Yellowwoods, IFC, and DEG. Naked's digital platform uses AI and automation to revolutionise insurance access, providing vehicle, home, and other insurance products. Proceeds support Naked's growth strategy including investment in automation and AI, product and market expansion, and enhanced advertising. DEG first invested in Naked in 2023 (Series B).
scope_basis: Equity in a digital insurance platform company.

title: Google — South Africa cloud region (Johannesburg), 2025
description: "Cabinet also welcomed the launch of Google South Africa's R2.5-billion cloud region in Johannesburg, which integrates South Africa into Google Cloud's global network. This project is Google's first in Africa and marks a significant investment in South Africa's technology infrastructure."

financier: Microsoft
title: Microsoft Azure South Africa — ZAR 20.4bn spent on the first enterprise datacentres (disclosed 2025)
description: At an event in Johannesburg on 6 March 2025, Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith announced a further ZAR 5.4 billion of cloud and AI infrastructure spending in South Africa by the end of 2027, and in doing so disclosed that this "builds on the company's ZAR 20.4 billion investment over the past three years to establish the nation's first enterprise-grade datacentres in Johannesburg and Cape Town". Moneyweb reported it as the first time Microsoft had publicly stated its South African datacentre investment, and put the combined figure at ZAR 25.8 billion. The Azure South Africa North (Johannesburg) and South Africa West (Cape Town) regions opened in March 2019 — the first enterprise-grade cloud datacentre regions on the continent — serving Azure, Office 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform from within South Africa. The forward ZAR 5.4bn half of the same announcement is held as 2025-03-06-microsoft-zaf-azure-expansion-2025-microsoft-azure-south-africa-zar-54b.
scope_basis: Spending is entirely on building enterprise cloud datacentres in Johannesburg and Cape Town.

financier: Microsoft
title: Microsoft Azure South Africa — ZAR 5.4B AI and Cloud Expansion 2025-2027
description: Microsoft announced ZAR 5.4 billion (approximately USD 295 million) to expand cloud and AI infrastructure in South Africa by end of 2027, announced by President Brad Smith on March 6, 2025 alongside President Cyril Ramaphosa. Includes construction of a second cloud infrastructure region in Centurion, expanded data centre capacity, power and water readiness, and AI skills development for government and private sector. Builds on the ZAR 20.4bn Microsoft states it invested over the preceding three years, held as 2025-03-06-microsoft-zaf-azure-microsoft-south-africa-datacentres-zar-204bn.
scope_basis: Cloud and AI infrastructure expansion, data centre capacity and AI skills.

financier: AlphaCode Venture Partners
title: AlphaCode Venture Partners — Moment Series A, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the source:

> Moment, a pan-African fintech, announced the close of its $22 million Series A funding round, led by AlphaCode Venture Partners, with continued investment from General Catalyst, MultiChoice, and fresh investment from Canal+. Since inception, Moment has raised $55 million to develop one of the Continent's most advanced payment infrastructure businesses, offering a comprehensive suite of payment collection and revenue retention solutions to corporate and enterprise merchants. The company will use the additional funding from this Series A round to deepen its network, enhance its platform and accelerate expansion across Africa.
scope_basis: Equity in a payments infrastructure fintech.

financier: MTN Group
title: MTN — South Africa ICT infrastructure investment, 2026
description: "Telecommunications operator MTN has pledged to invest 21.8 billion South African rand (US$1.3 billion) over the next three years to expand ICT infrastructure and advance the digital economy in South Africa." "The announcement was made at the annual South Africa Investment Conference in Sandton, Johannesburg, this week." "By the end of 2028, it expects to invest a total of almost R22 billion ($1.3 billion) in the country." MTN SA spent R6.8 billion ($404 million) on its network in 2025.
scope_basis: A mobile operator's investment in its own ICT and network infrastructure.

financier: Oakvale Invest
title: Oakvale Invest — Tennsa, 2026
description: "South African startup Tennsa, an AI business intelligence platform built for SMEs, has become the first portfolio company of Oakvale Invest, Africa's first AI-focused pre-seed fund." "The startup has now become the first investment of Oakvale Invest, which has invested more than ZAR1 million (US$61,000) in the company."
scope_basis: Pre-seed equity in an AI business intelligence start-up.

financier: Pepkor
title: Pepkor — Shop2Shop/Flash merger into FintechCo, 2026
description: "Retail giant Pepkor has merged Flash, its wholly-owned fintech subsidiary, with Shop2Shop to create merchant commerce and fintech platform FintechCo, with annual throughput exceeding R200 billion." "Pepkor will acquire a controlling 57.1% interest in FintechCo through a combination of a R1.57 billion cash subscription for new shares in Shop2Shop and the contribution of its entire 100% shareholding in Flash, which has been valued at R10.6 billion." "The proposed transaction is subject to various conditions precedent, which include, but are not limited to, receiving all necessary regulatory and competition authority approvals." Pepkor states an ambition "to build a leading digital bank with a nationwide distribution footprint" and plans "a planned future listing of FintechCo".
scope_basis: Cash subscription for shares in a merchant commerce and fintech platform.

financier: Telkom
title: Telkom — Telkom AI Institute (South Africa), 2026
description: "Telkom pledges USD 6.1 million to establish the Telkom AI Institute, a platform designed to equip South Africans with AI and digital skills, foster innovation, and accelerate inclusive participation in the digital economy." The pledge was one of several announced as ITU's Partner2Connect Digital Coalition surpassed US$100 billion in commitments at the WSIS Forum 2026 in Geneva.
scope_basis: Pledge establishes an institute for AI and digital skills.

financier: Equinix
title: Equinix — South Africa data centre expansion, 2026
description: "Global data centre operator Equinix Inc. is expanding in South Africa with a planned $438 million investment, as it seeks to tap into growing demand for artificial intelligence and cloud services across Africa." "The company... said it will build additional facilities in Johannesburg and Cape Town." "Sandile Dube, Equinix's managing director for South Africa, said the company has secured about 327,000 square metres of land for future development. The expansion is expected to add roughly 160 megawatts of data centre capacity." "All investments are funded by our own balance sheet." Per the companion report, Equinix "has bought more land in that city and also in Cape Town, totalling R890 million."
scope_basis: Investment is entirely in new data centre facilities and land for them.

financier: Microsoft
title: Microsoft South Africa — $329M Data Centre and AI Expansion 2026
description: Microsoft announced a $329 million investment in South Africa in April 2026 to expand data centres, boost infrastructure resilience, and develop AI skills. Covers land acquisition for future data centre expansion, power and water readiness improvements, and capacity increases at existing Johannesburg and Cape Town facilities. Described as building on an earlier $1.2 billion total commitment to South Africa.
scope_basis: Data-centre expansion with land, power and water readiness for those facilities, plus AI skills.

title: ZamStats: Increased availability of relevant statistics, 2025-2028 (Statistics Sweden)
description:
Support to ZamStats to strengthen the management of ZamStats, the coordination of the National Statistical System, methodological capacity in economic, agriculture, environment and social statistics. Project overall outcome Enhanced capacity to produce statistics in line with user needs, sound statistical methods and international standards. Component 2: Coordination Component objective/outcome: A strengthened National Statistical System (NSS) that fosters stronger interagency collaborations to improve data integration, sharing, and dissemination across key government entities. Component 3: Statistical Methodology Component objective/outcome: Enhanced methodological capacity Component 4: Economic Statistics Component objective/outcome: Enhanced capacity for ZamStats to produce timely and relevant economic statistics. Component 5: Agriculture, Environment and Social Statistics Component objective/outcome 1: Agricultural and Environment statistics contributes to evidenced based decision-making on food security in the country. Component objective/outcome 2: Household Budget Survey is produced to inform the users on critical socio-economic, agricultural and environment indicators.
scope_basis: Capacity support to the national statistics agency and a household budget survey.

financier: UNESCO
title: Supporting Digital Skills for Next Generation
description: The project aims to strengthen digital education in Zambia by piloting a hub school model in Lusaka Province. The initiative focuses on building teachers' and learners' digital capacity, equipping the school with modern technologies, and ensuring equitable access, especially for girls and disadvantaged groups. Key outputs include a computer lab, smart classrooms, digital pedagogy training, and locally relevant learning content.
